item: The error journal's trim swaps a finished temp over the file instead of truncating it in place (R175 part 1)
summary: Before: past 512 KiB the trim of data/app_errors.jsonl read the file and wrote the newest 2,000 lines back over it with write_text, which empties the file first: a crash inside it left no journal and a second process appending between the read and the write lost its line (read from the code; not reproduced in the field). Now the trim writes <file>.tmp.<pid>.<thread> beside it, fsyncs, and os.replace moves it over; a failed swap removes its own temp; a temp left by a process that no longer runs is swept by the next trim (psutil; where it is missing nothing is swept). The kept lines are the same bytes. Tests: 5 new, 3 red with the in-place write put back (a process killed at the swap leaves the old file whole; two writers never share a temp name; a failed swap leaves the journal and no temp). An append by another process between the read and the swap can still be lost (the lost-append window is not closed by this; it needs a lock across processes or a rule that two processes do not share a data dir, R175 part 2).
